items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: David Baker was there and he is a few years older than me but he’s like my big brother and he’s always looked out for me. In fact when I went to Yale University we were roommates.

ctx.x: Was jazz, before this seeing Ray Brown, was jazz part of your household?

Oh yes. My parents were into Duke Ellington, Count Basie. My mother’s youngest brother was into the more current stuff like with the bebop and stuff like that. And all these musicians around town, you know, like were all very supportive. There are so many names I hesitate to name a lot of names, but I mentioned the main ones like the Montgomery brothers and David Baker. Can you imagine that any of them could envision where that led? You know this gathering here is astounding to me.

items.title: David N. Baker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I’ve tried to be pretty much [of] a mentor to Larry... He has studied with me from time to time... We’re in a quintet which consisted of Joe Kennedy and myself... Larry Ridley...

ctx.x: In the Jazz Review [September 1959]. Down here, he had written a – when he wrote the article, he talked about some of us that he was really interested in. We ultimately got invited – I got the Dizzy Gillespie Scholarship and some other people got scholarships for us to come to the Lenox, to the School of Jazz in ’59. I took him to hear Wes while he was here. He couldn’t believe that. It was Wes Montgomery, Paul Parker, and Melvin Rhyne. They were playing at an after-hours club called the Missile Room, which was…

there that year. I just remember it took us forever, because we were driving a raggedy- ass car that Kiger had. We’d have to stop and get gas and oil at so many places. So we got to Lenox late. We were coming up there as the fair-haired boys. We were going to be the heroes. Gunther had raved about us. We could all play. We figured, boy, when we get there, we’re going to turn that place inside out. Unfortunately, Ornette got there two days before us and upset the place. There were people who were pro-Ornette:…
